content: The provided text is a list of references and citations from various scientific studies, reports, and publications. It includes detailed bibliographic information about research on topics such as vector control, sterile insect techniques, dengue prevention, genetic modification of mosquitoes, and cost-effectiveness analyses in public health. 1. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) hosted a symposium in 1981 in Neuherberg, Germany, focusing on the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) and the application of radiation in genetic insect control. This event highlighted advancements in pest control methodologies. 2. Liyanage et al. (2019) conducted an evaluation of intensified dengue control measures in the Panadura Medical Officer of Health division in Sri Lanka. Using interrupted time series analysis, the study assessed the effectiveness and cost-efficiency of these interventions, with findings published in The Lancet Planetary Health. 3. Lofgren et al. (1974) explored the release of chemosterilized male mosquitoes for controlling Anopheles albimanus populations in El Salvador. Their field methods and population control strategies were detailed in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 4. Lorimer, Lounibos, and Petersen (1976) conducted field trials using a translocation homozygote in Aedes aegypti to facilitate population replacement. Their findings were published in the Journal of Economic Entomology. 5. Lutrat et al. (2019) discussed the potential of sex-sorting technologies for pest control in their article titled It’s Raining Men. published in Trends in Parasitology. The study emphasized the importance of male-only releases in SIT programs. 6. MacDonald (1952) provided foundational insights into the measurement of malaria transmission, which remain relevant in epidemiological studies today. This work was published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society of Medicine. 7. Rodrigues Mayne et al. (2019) investigated the optimal gamma radiation sterilization dose for adult male Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Their findings contribute to the refinement of SIT protocols. 8. Massad et al. (2018) modeled the risk of urban yellow fever resurgence in American cities infested with Aedes mosquitoes. Their study, published in Epidemiology and Infection, underscores the importance of vector control in urban settings. 9. McMeniman et al. (2009) successfully introduced a life-shortening Wolbachia infection into Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, demonstrating its potential for vector control. This breakthrough was published in Science. 10. Murray et al. (1996) developed the Global Burden of Disease framework, which provides a comprehensive assessment of mortality and disability from diseases and injuries. This work has been instrumental in public health planning and policy. 11. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published numerous guidelines and frameworks, including the 2009 dengue guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and control, as well as the 2014 guidance framework for testing genetically modified mosquitoes. 12. Reiter and Nathan (2001) provided guidelines for assessing the efficacy of insecticidal space sprays for controlling Aedes aegypti, the primary vector of dengue. These guidelines were published by the WHO. 13. Salomon et al. (2012) conducted a study on disability weights for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2010, providing a standardized approach to assessing health outcomes from diseases and injuries. 14. Schaffner and Mathis (2014) reviewed the history and future scenarios of dengue and its vectors in the WHO European Region, emphasizing the need for proactive vector control measures. 15. The Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity (2000) introduced the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, which addresses the safe handling and use of living modified organisms. 16. Sinkins (2004) explored the role of Wolbachia and cytoplasmic incompatibility in mosquito populations, highlighting its potential for vector control. This research was published in Insect Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. 17. Vanlerberghe et al. (2009) conducted a cluster-randomized trial to evaluate community involvement in dengue vector control, demonstrating the effectiveness of participatory approaches. 18. Vreysen et al. (2000) documented the successful eradication of Glossina austeni (tsetse fly) on Unguja Island, Zanzibar, using the SIT. This achievement was published in the Journal of Economic Entomology. 19. WHO (2017) released a comprehensive global vector control response strategy for 2017–2030, emphasizing integrated approaches to vector management. 20. WHO (2018) published a manual on the prevention and control of invasive mosquito species in the European Region, providing technical guidance for public health authorities.
